_doc.what: Variant of config-sample.json showing a HERD REGISTRY with three vendors side by side: agy (Antigravity/Gemini), opencode, and pi. Read config-sample.json first for the full key guide, and config-sample-cli-executors.json for the different `cli` seam. Copy the `herding` block into your own .bee/config.json; the `models` block below is one example of pointing a tier slot at one of these herds.
_doc.seam: `herding.agents` is the WRITE-WORK executor registry: a named entry is what `bee herding run` / `--continue` / `bee herding wave` spawns into a herdr pane as a real cell-execution worker in its own worktree. It is NOT the `cli` tier shape (that one is gather-only and pipes a prompt through stdin). A herd name always means the pane transport.
_doc.entry_shape: Each entry is either a plain argv token array, or {"argv": [...], "env": {...}, "workspace_trust": {...}}. TOKEN 0 IS THE HERDR AGENT KIND, passed straight through to `herdr agent start --kind <token0>` with no bee-side allow-list; every remaining token becomes that agent's own argv after `--`. herdr 0.8.2 accepts these kinds: pi, claude, codex, gemini, cursor, devin, agy, cline, omp, mastracode, opencode, copilot, kimi, kiro, droid, amp, grok, hermes, kilo, qodercli, qwen, maki. So `opencode` and `pi` need no bee change at all — they only need an entry here.
_doc.the_one_rule: Put each vendor's DO-NOT-ASK flag in its entry. An agent that stops to ask anything mid-run — a permission prompt, a trust prompt — stalls the pane until the idle timeout, and a human keystroke into a live worker pane hijacks the agent's turn. Per vendor: claude `--permission-mode bypassPermissions`; agy `--dangerously-skip-permissions`; opencode `--auto` (auto-approve permissions not explicitly denied); pi `-a` / `--approve` (pi has no permission popups at all — it runs with the user's own permissions — but an interactive session in a project holding project-local settings, packages, or extensions asks whether to TRUST them, and `-a` answers that for the run).
_doc.env: `env` (herd-registry D4) is exported into the freshly split pane as one `export K='v'` line, after the split and before the agent starts, so the agent process inherits it. Keys must match [A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]* and values must be newline-free; ANY violation drops the WHOLE entry. Use it for a provider key you do not want in your shell profile — never commit a real key into a repo.
_doc.workspace_trust: `workspace_trust` (herd-registry D5) is for a vendor whose trust decision lives in a JSON file holding an ARRAY of trusted directories: bee pre-seeds the fresh worktree path into that array before the spawn, so the agent never meets a trust dialog. agy is the live case. opencode needs nothing here. pi keeps its decisions in ~/.pi/agent/trust.json keyed BY DIRECTORY, not as a flat array, so it does not fit this shape — that is exactly why the pi entries below carry `-a` instead.
_doc.models_example: `{"kind": "herding", "agent": "<name>"}` on a tier slot routes that slot's work through a pane running that herd. `"fallback": "default"` re-dispatches a failed run (spawn failure, timeout, invalid result) through the runtime's own default model path; without it a failure stays loud and the pane is kept as forensics. The registry is inert until a slot, a `--agent` flag, or a string `herding.agent_command` names an entry — safe to keep in every repo.
_doc.models_are_placeholders: The `-m` / `--model` values below are EXAMPLES. Run `opencode models` and `pi --list-models` and replace them with ids your own accounts actually carry.
_doc.try_one: bee herding run --agent opencode-auto --task 'say PONG and stop' --cwd <a worktree path> --json
